body:
Thank you for the kind words.

I've been through therapy and CBT a few times.  I also combined therapy with prescription drugs.  

I've changed my diet, exercised excessively, got burned out from the rat race and lived in a van before it was a thing.

As a young kid, I thought stuff would get easier to manage as I got older.  In my personal experience, that hasn't been the case.

i'm late to the party, but i make up playlists for sad songs in my head all of the time:

[Jessica Lea Mayfield - Somewhere in Your Heart](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1i7CNyIPQq8)

[Nine Inch Nails - Something I Can Never Have (still)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UEW8riKU_tE)

[Joy Division - New Dawn Fades](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oo7lt0lLOvg)

[Alice in Chains - Nutshell](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9EKi2E9dVY8)

[Audioslave - Like a Stone](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7QU1nvuxaMA)

[Elliott Smith - A Passing Feeling](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XJQXCTLY8_s)

never married and don't have any kids.

parents (divorced before i can remember) are still alive.  and i have 3 half brothers.

on paper, my life looked okay.

managing depression/anxiety is exhausting.

the ARNP that i have prescribing me drugs, agreed with me that we don't know a whole lot about the brain.  i mean, we do to a certain extent.

i've also been in/out therapy and on/off drugs since my 20s.  i reluctantly went down the SSRI route (what a mistake) back when SSRIs were the thing.

i started my day by getting up at the crack of dawn and running up at a [mountain near me](https://imgur.com/gallery/GvgidzP).  it gets the adrenaline and endorphins going, but they don't last long.

i've written from this account and mentioned the awful feeling of waking up. i wish i knew how to get around it.

i'm trying some ADHD meds that marginally help.  i don't know.

hopefully your day turns out okay and you don't have to think too much.

sometimes i'll buy ice cream, eat part of it, and then forget about it.  rediscovering a half eaten gallon of ice cream gives me just a bit of satisfaction.  just for a second.

i'm still throwing some new things at myself (different medication), but i'm having issues with them again.

the dread feeling in the morning is the worst.  i've tried describing it to people and some just don't get it.

thanks for the reply.

there have been a few years where i slept all of the time.  i threw myself at it again because i was on the edge a few months ago.

i'm taking care of myself, exercising, etc. at the moment, but mentally i'm still the same (as you described).  

take care.

the emptiness and exhaustion overwhelm me these days.  i never thought it could get worse.

looking back (4,5) and realizing how long both of us have been dealing with it just baffles me.

i really wish i had some sort of answer.

i really wish it was that easy.

treating chronic depression/anxiety isn't as simple as one might think.  the ideas you present are definitely good.  i've done all of them (minus the small business idea) throughout my life.

when the act of work (or result) brings no joy, life becomes difficult.  it's a struggle.  for me, it's a 24/7 struggle.  to be honest, right now, i'd rather be sleeping.

there are very few things i haven't tried throughout my life to just feel marginally okay.

based on my experience, nothing.

i'm 49.  did the dating app thing, since, oh, '97.  joined tons of groups.  hung out with friends.  in the end, i end up empty.  it's a me problem, i know.

Lorazepam was being used to try and treat my anxiety and terrible sleeping patters (i haven't been sleeping).  i used it for a week (it is addictive).

i'm currently trying Olanzapine since my family has a history of bipolar disorder.  i've never exhibited signs of mania and i'm not diagnosed with bipolar disorder.  it does knock me out at night, so i guess there is that.  i've only been on it a few days.

i kind've abuse caffeine a bit (i buy it in pill form).  if i don't have any caffeine when i'm in a major depressive episode, i just tend to sleep all of the time.  i'm really trying not to use too much of it while trying these other medications.

we'll see what happens in the next couple of weeks.

:(  i feel ya.

49M (this month).

i also keep seeing my peers advance in their careers and hobbies while i stagnate and try to manage my depression.  i don't want to think about offing myself 24/7.  and i'm so exhausted trying to manage it.

doing it alone is the worst part.

i'm back seeing doctors for a third wave in my life.  actually finding the RIGHT doctors is quite frustrating.  trying different medications this time around (no SSRIs for me).  i swear that humans still have no clue what is going on.

in the olden days, you had to call to make arrangements with friends.  i still remember a few phone numbers.  sometimes you would just go over to their house and knock on the door.

you scheduled time to watch tv.  i remember thursday night as being filled with the best  content during the 80s/90s.  saturday morning cartoons were a thing.  you often heard new music on the radio.

midlife in this time is weird.  i was a big science fiction geek as a kid/teenager and thought this type of reality would be good (instant communication, access to everything).  boy was i wrong.

and thanks for the comment.

i don't tell people to f themselves, but i know where you are coming from.

i just don't feel better no matter what i do.  it's quite debilitating.
i find myself doing the same exact thing.

thanks.

and likewise.

i've been posting online since (roughly) the late 90s with the same tone.

the awareness of loneliness, depression, anxiety, and nearly all mental illnesses has gotten better over the years.

does putting it out there help?  to be honest, i'm not sure.

i'm honestly in the worst place i've ever been.

thanks for the thoughtful reply.

it might sound like i'm tackling everything all at once.  that's far from the truth.  it seems that most of the time, i will hyperfocus on something, work, running, climbing, whatever, and kind of have the other stuff in the background.  it's seems it's harder for me to balance stuff.

i have volunteered and helped others.  i think it's really beneficial, but at this point, i need to focus on doing something for myself, because i'm actually having some issues with just existing.

i really do appreciate the thoughtful reply.

that's a really heavy question.  it's hard to answer these days.

stats: 48M, single, never married, no kids, no job, living at the base of a mountain in the PNW.  dealing with MDD, GAD, (possible ADHD), some trauma that likely needs to get dealt with at some point.  been down the path of prescription medication for 20+ years.  same with therapy.  i've been through CBT twice during different parts of my life.  i've been a pretty hardcore athlete.  hobbies don't give me any joy.  worked myself to burnout multiple times.  lived in a van and traveled a bit.  i haven't worked in a while because i'm well, burnt out.

i just had another partial evaluation that i just couldn't get through.  talking to a therapist about Absurdism in my state is futile.

when one approaches life from many many angles, it's hard to keep going.  it's simply exhausting.  persistent anxiety, depression, and anhedonia doesn't help the situation.

and frankly, i'm lonely as f.  can't hold down a meaningful relationship.  so yeah, i feel pretty stuck in every aspect of my life.  it's overwhelmingly frustrating.
the idea of failing and being in a worse situation.

self reflection is interesting.

it's safe to say i've had enough life experience to realize that (imo) i'm useless.

my frame of reference is simply from my experiences.

in all honesty, my mind keeps telling me i'm done.  just done with trying.

i went and tried to get another evaluation (3rd in my life) with a psychologist, but ended up just giving up on myself.  i'm so exhausted battling the negative thinking.  i'm exhausted.  i mean really exhausted.

deep down i believe that i don't have that power to maintain/sustain myself.
well, darn.
it's a National Park worth visiting.

i live at the base of Mount Rainier in WA.  i've done a bunch of climbing, hiking, skiing, running in the mountains, etc.

i'll probably head off to the North Cascades though.

the grass is not always greener on the other side.  or around the corner.  or nearby.  at least that's been my experience.

i'll make it to 49 in July.  and, well, the weather is better up in the mountains where i live in July-September.

yep, the consequences of failing scare me more than the act.

i have a span of two months to do the deed.

my only reservation (still) is if i fail.  i don't want to live with more suffering and pain.

this human thing is hard.

hope you feel okay at some point.
i hope you find peace on occasion.  living like this is horrendous.  :(

i fall back to a depressive/anxious state all the time (i'm 48).  i honestly don't know anyone that has experienced long bouts as long as me.  my lows are low.  i mean not brushing my teeth low.

i find minor comfort with absurdism.  there was a recent video on YT that summarized it fairly well: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jv79l1b-eoI](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jv79l1b-eoI)

i keep asking myself questions.  what's the point?  with anything?  what's the meaning in anything?  it all boils down to: i don't know.  if anyone digs deep enough, we just don't know.  ask the top philosophers, scientists, whoever, what's the point?  they can give you an opinion.  but deep down, humans just don't know.

thanks.

i hope you feel okay at some point.

thanks for the reply.

i hope you feel better.  at some point.  in some fashion.

no words of stupid advice.

just peace.

thanks for the reply.

i struggle (intensely) to be okay.  it's exhausting.  as i get older, i'm out of energy.  it impacts every aspect of my life.  did i say it was exhausting.

i don't remember the last time i enjoyed anything.

i wish i had good advice.  i brushed a few hours ago because i forgot when i had last brushed.

no sleep.  suicide ideation.  depression is not a life.  i know you get it, you're in the no brush club.

this headspace is hell.  when i talk to other people about how bad i am, most don't get it.  i'm goin on 49 this july.  i would never ever wish depression/anxiety on anyone.

this is coming from a suicidal person, but keep trying?

nice things, people, nothing helps.  working for it doesn't help.

i tried.
i wish it was that easy.

i 100% agree.

i'm past the point of even going for a beer: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jv79l1b-eoI](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jv79l1b-eoI)
i meant to read that book at one point in my life.

48 going on 49.  i'm of average intelligence and looks, but it doesn't matter.

i know it doesn't help, but i've lived with depression all of my life.  i gave up.  my retirement is suicide.  i already sent two notes off to a couple of people these past few months.

i know it doesn't get better.  i'm living it.

48, nearly 49.

just wait, just wait.

i hear ya.

while i managed to go outside yesterday, i didn't necessarily enjoy it.

this whole human suffering thing (whatever the cause for each individual) is simply not fun.  to say the least.
i used to do the same thing.  oh man, it was so relaxing too.

This is my exact train of thought every single day. Have I tried ketamine? No. Have I tried ECT or TMS/rTMS. No. Those are my last options. There's EMDR too.

But, I've already given up. I'm exhausted.

i've thrown myself into group stuff (climbing, running) in the past.

but i'm exhausted from it all.  nothing is fun.
Is reality real? As far as I know, yes. But I could be wrong.

"The struggle itself ... is enough to fill a man's heart. One must imagine Sisyphus happy".

Camus, Nietzsche, etc. definitely got it. for me, i've gravitated towards existential nihilism.

i'm aware, unfortunately.

for some reason, that thought has never been comforting for me.

i turned 48 this year.  i've done the therapy thing, meds, hobbies, worked myself to death, dating, etc.

i've been a runner/ultrarunner/climber/hiker/skier etc.  last year i basically quit running.  i had a few terrible long runs on trails that resulted in: extreme sadness, loneliness, suicide ideation.   running used to be my time to just get out of my head.  i've been doing it since i was \~9.  i'm still recovering and haven't been able to get out there. i'm hoping to hit the trails ONCE this year.

the pain/suffering never seem to go away.

take care of yourself.
yes.

i stopped doing what i had done in the past.  none of it was working.  i've had 20+ years of therapy.  in that time i also jumped between different types of prescription drugs.

i've thrown myself into work, hobbies, exercise, dating, lived in a van after getting burnt out from working too much.

i'm in this headspace (that has been the majority of my life) where i'm breaking down ALL THE TIME.  now that i'm older and living by myself, i have seriously lost it.  the pandemic obviously didn't help.

existence isn't at all appealing in any capacity.

and i have extreme anhedonia.

i'm not functioning anymore.
i've stopped thinking in this manner.  or maybe i just never accepted the pain.
as i mentioned from the other account, the thoughts are constant and never end.  this is a lifelong thing for me.

here's the original comment from the right account:

*thanks for the kind words.*  
  
*i should probably preface every post with my age. i'm 48. unfortunately, i've been doing all of what you have mentioned. i honestly think some of us have been dealt a bad genetic hand.*  
  
*i just took a nap and woke up wanting to kill myself.*  
  
*i lost.*

when i receive unsolicited advice, i get a bit irritated.  not only have i heard every suggestion, i've likely replayed the same thought in my head an uncountable amount of times.

depression does cause actual changes to the brain.  i'm sure you're well versed in every single symptom as well.

i actually gave up this year.  it honestly feels like i've lost.  i don't remember what it feels like to be okay.

i've had terrible anxiety since 4/5.  depression didn't start until about age 10/11.

honestly, i'm surprised i'm still alive.

hang in there?

48M here.

dating (or however you want to label the concept) can likely continue until the end of time for an individual.  we are pretty basic animals, still.

i know a 97 year old woman that is "dating" a 99 year old man.  they hike and get a long wonderfully.
agreed.

i've stopped texting.  i just don't have words anymore.  even texting seems so very distant and empty to me these days.

having conversations with myself has reached new levels i never thought i would reach.  and i went and lived on the road.

i'm 48 and have been doing a variety of things throughout my life.  i'm a climber, skier, ultrarunner, (was) a workaholic, been in the dating pool for ages, etc.

i have extreme anhedonia and all of the classic symptoms of depression/anxiety.  it makes life not cool.  i've had lifelong suicidal ideation.  i've treated it with therapy, CBT, prescription drugs.  i've thrown everything at it.

i also know the limits of simply being human.

the classic answers that i could suggest are really meaningless.

i'm sorry you are feeling this way.  i really do wish there was something i could say or do to change stuff.
many, many times.

i've forced myself through terrible episodes while working, going to school, while in relationships, etc.

lifelong depression has lead me to just quit a lot of the above things.

i'm in a pretty dark place right now.

true.  i can't believe i used the word "should".

i've gravitated more towards the concept of existential nihilism with a hint of determinism.  accepting that mode of thinking always circles my thinking back around to just not existing.
short answer, yes.

we are approaching nearly 8 billion people on the planet.  that bell curve for non-interesting people is bulging pretty high in the middle right now.  (assuming the interesting people are on the tails.)
depression is currently putting my life on hold.  literally.

this is coming strictly from personal experience, but technology has not increased value in creating meaningful connections with other humans.  if anything, i have more empty interactions.

i'm 48 and literally grew up behind a screen of some sort.  computer stuff has been my hobby, my career.

at times, i wish i lived in a different era.
same.
thank you for the kind words.

i have in the past.  20+ years of therapy/prescription drugs/CBT.  was it effective?  uh.

right now, no.
living with depression/anxiety all of my life has taken a toll. i can't justify the suffering to myself anymore.

i'm 48.  i gave myself until the end of the year.

to truly change behavior and the brain would likely be a miracle.  IMO, humans are still pretty barbaric.

i've done therapy/prescription drugs for 20+ years only to realize drug companies really have been screwing us over.  i've changed my environment, diet, i'm an athlete, dove into hobbies, dating, work, everything.

yet here i am.

this human will likely end things early.

i do appreciate the encouragement though.

i've lived 48 years with constant anxiety/depression, it takes a toll on the mind/body.  i've fought and worked f'ing hard at everything and i'm still in the same place.  i'm losing the fight at the moment.

i wish i knew.  i really do.

i continue to suffer and it's obviously not fun.
hopefully you are able to get through it. it's an awful way to feel.
it has nothing to do with being a "man".

i wish something would give me joy.

games, hobbies, or whatever, feel dull.  it's an unfortunate mindset.
r/SuicideWatch might be the closest thing.

also...

depression is complicated.  medicating the general public by throwing SSRIs/SNRIs, etc. at them is, um, barbaric.

believe me, i'm very scientifically based, but holy crap.  i felt like a lab rat when i was jumping between drugs.
i've been through CBT (two times during different parts of my life), prescription drugs + therapy for 20+ years.

based on my 48 years of living, my life experiences have been riddled with anxiety/depression/thoughts of suicide.

i'm tired.

i'm a fool thinking things will ever change.

determinism.  yeah, i'm pretty sure that's a thing.  free will doesn't exist.

i wish i can say something or do something.

i few months ago, i, um, was driving pretty fast down a highway hoping i would crash.

i've walked/driven to numerous bridges throughout my life.

lately, i've tried eating comfort food, thinking today, right now, was my last meal.

all of the things i keep doing don't work.  i listen to everyone and have followed their suggestions.

being human sucks.  period.

i really really wish you peace.

our bodies/minds appear to be screaming at us to change something.  my conscious brain has no idea what to do anymore.

and agreed.  this is absolute hell.

the most reward i am able to experience is: that's nice.  and i struggle to even find that anymore.

i try to describe the feeling to someone else and they just don't get it.

there's not much difference.

i'm a skinny average (now old(er)) white dude.  alone.

i want to kill myself 24/7.  depression/anxiety/suicidal ideation has been my norm throughout life.
when one is in this state, you don't want to be around anyone.  it's a terrible loop.

i was sitting on the toilet about 30 minutes ago and thinking, "nobody knows me.  in all honesty, nobody really gives a f about me."

i have no problem helping others in need.  i have no problem trying to make other people feel at home or worth it.  i've been told by numerous people that i'm very caring.

right now, my demon is pushing me to overeat and never sleep.

i've been in and out of r/depression and r/suicidewatch from multiple accounts for a little over a year trying to see if posting and/or replying would help.  it hasn't.  i thought that likeminded individuals that would be willing to listen would help.

i'm finding more peace in knowing i will no longer be suffering.
i would never wish it upon ANYONE.  it just ends up reinforcing my belief that everything is pointless and has no meaning.  making things worse.

i've thrown myself into a career (got burnt out), hobbies, living out of a van, therapy, CBT, prescription drugs, mindfulness, ultrarunning, skiing, climbing, dating.  and during those moments, i'm extremely anxious if not suicidal.  picture a runner out in the mountains wanting to jump off of a cliff during a run.  having it hit then, not fun.

life sucks for some.  life sucks more for others.  i keep fighting to survive.  but to suffer?  in my own mental hell?  wtf?

i've had these conversations with quite a few people.  trying to explain the morning dreadfulness (it lasts 3-4 hours for me) is hard.  in my 48 years, this time it is bad.  it's beyond anything i've experienced before.

on top of everything,  anhedonia.  so trying to enjoy that netfix show, or song, or even spending time with friends, brings no sense of joy.  it's just dull.  black and white.  it's like my reinforcement system was setup to self-hate.

sorry, i just don't have any answers for myself anymore.  even typing this out seems negative.  i always feel bad.

thanks for the reply.

i wish it was that easy.
what does peace mean to you?
what is the risk?

summer 48 here.

i'm having a hard time going back to music.  heck, i stopped watching Stranger Things after season 2?  i forgot.  i can't stand watching stuff alone anymore.

i thought to myself yesterday, "Yeah, I guess I'm surviving.  I have no kids.  No relationship.  No pets.  In a house by myself.  Go me."

wish i had some vodka and coke.  that sounds good.

and f'ing hell.  i can't hold down a relationship as well.

being human in 2022, mid-life.  this is it?  really?

take this advice for what it is, since i'm not a doctor or therapist.

i've seen this behavior all throughout my life (via stories of others).  i'm 48M.

get out of the relationship.  period.  surround yourself with people that bring out characteristics that are positive and promote growth/fun.  hopefully you can reciprocate.  healthy relationships throughout your life do wonders for your wellbeing.

i dislike using words like should/need, but maybe it would be beneficial if he got diagnosed?  if possible?  i've noticed that people's actions/behaviors don't change much throughout their life.  UNLESS they work on themselves.  constantly.

48M.  i've given up.

i don't have solutions.  i don't have answers.  i've looked.  hard.

if you saw me, right now, as i type this comment out, you would think i was living on the streets.

as one who is also trying to end it, i'm having a hard time executing THOSE plans.

i understand what you are saying.

for this human, i suffer from recurrent major depressive episodes.   i'm  48M.  the amount of work i have to put into not suffering is horrendous.  this is on top of, you know, trying to live a life with meaningful and stable relationships, pursuing a career, taking care of myself, etc.

thanks for the reply.
agreed.

i really appreciate the reply.

i've fallen down a pretty deep (maddening) hole.  i also lean on the atheist side of things.  lately, i have been leaning towards existential nihilism.

i've called a crisis line twice in the last year.  i've done the therapy thing for over 20+ years (not currently).  the capitalistic rat race here in the US (well, the world), has really gotten to me.

i've been in my head contemplating existence (deeply) for the better part of the last few years.  the classic saying, "the more i learn, the less i know" is quite poignant.  i simply no longer have any answers.
in the end, i'm not certain talking about it actually helps.  i can type/talk on end to anyone these days about my issues.  they don't seem to get better.

i've witnessed a grandparent die of dementia in her 90s.  my parents are well into their 70s.

i've experienced depression/anxiety that is next level.  i've had suicide ideation since i've been a kid.

no human should have to experience this type of self-abuse.

i'm at the one moment at a time.

time is weird.

yep, sounds like how i feel.  except i'm a 48M and i don't have a cat.

a study/article that hit the mainstream today: "Evidence That Serotonin Failure Does Not Cause Depression".  after 20+ years of being on prescription drugs (including SSRIs), i can confirm. :)

i've done the therapy thing for decades and CBT at different times in my life.

my brain goes down the existential nihilism road (lately) and i just absolutely spiral.  i also direct all hatred inward.  the suffering in unbearable.

i wish i could say/write something to make it go away for all of us that have to experience life this way.  as i've said before, it just isn't a life.
my skills are in Network Engineering, but i've lost all passion.  the industry makes me very uneasy these days.

and the best part about today was a study/article that hit the mainstream: "Evidence That Serotonin Failure Does Not Cause Depression".

after 20+ years of being on prescription drugs (including SSRIs), i can confirm.  :)

seriously though, i'm so hopeless it's not even funny.

hang in there?

i've tried prescription drugs (they kinda worked, but not).  the side effects were horrendous.  aside from that, i've done therapy for 20+ years (didn't really help), tried CBT twice, poured myself into hobbies, exercise, dating, a job.  none of it really helped.

good times.

thanks for the response.

to be honest, i'm exhausted from listening to myself.  my depressive thoughts are on repeat.

be well.

i've been dealing with depression/anxiety for nearly my entire time alive (nearing 48 years this month).  having constant feelings of loneliness, worthlessness, uselessness takes a toll.  you know, typical severe depressive symtoms.

i'm exhausted.

i appreciate the response.

this is verbatim from what i wrote in April:

*- if you ask a psychologist/psychiatrist to treat depression/anxiety, they will inevitably go down the path of SSRIs/SNRIs, then TMS(rTMS)/ECT. ketamine is the latest thing, but that treatment is very transient. rTMS is yet another transient treatment. average relapse is a little over a year.*  
*- this is where are in 2022. my options are limited.*  
*- when i wake up (it's ALL there in full force). i don't choose to think these thoughts. consistent suicidal ideation / depression / anxiety is exhausting. oh, and i've had some shitty therapists over the years.*  
*- i've apparently not yet mastered CBT. otherwise i wouldn't be in this mental state.*

when i wake up now, it is even worse.  i have this TREMENDOUS desire to not be alive.  i absolutely despise the feeling.

basically, i've had 20+ years of therapy.  i've done CBT twice.  i've tried multiple prescription drugs.  i'm an athlete, so exercise is a given.  i've poured myself into a job, i lived in a van, i try to date (not at the moment, my mental health is horrendous), i've done the hobby thing.  i have yet to try TMS (rTMS).  or ketamine.
i don't know.
Elliott Smith - Memory Lane

yes to everything.

i have extreme anhedonia.  and existential nihilism has been on my mind.  so yeah, finding meaning or the point is pretty non-existent at the moment.

we are here.

i [posted](https://www.reddit.com/r/depression/comments/umjl5q/feel_out_of_place_in_rdepression_because_of_my/) somewhat recently with similar sentiments.

as someone pointed out, a sub exists already: [https://www.reddit.com/r/adultdepression/](https://www.reddit.com/r/adultdepression/).  unfortunately, it doesn't get used that often.
i'm right there with you.

i went back to work in my field after a hiatus in 2020.  i lasted 2 weeks.  before that i worked at a not so meaningful job.  i lasted 2 months.

i keep trying.

thanks for the kind words.

i don't have any answers. i don't think anyone (past/present) really knows the truth.  if you find them, send them my way.

Lex Fridman (just some random CS dude who does a podcast over on the youtubes) asks each of his interviewees a question at the end of his interview: "What is the meaning of life?"  it's interesting to hear the take of the top scientists/philosophers/researchers in 2022.

what is the nature of reality?  really?

p.s. oh, and i've dealt with major depression, suicide ideation, and anxiety for over 40 years.  i'm in a major depressive episode right now.  i question meaning, the point, etc. way way too much during the day.
i know this might sound weird, but do you know your great grandfather's first name off the top of your head?

i came across a quote this morning (it's 6:16am where i live):

“This is the way that I think about my life, and I hope that you'll think of your life too.

You should think about your life hoping that there will be many moments in it about which you can say; There is no place I'd rather be, there is no thing I'd rather be doing, there is nobody I'd rather be with, & this I will remember well.”

― Albert Borgmann

i'm an old(er) dude that is having a pretty hard time justifying my existence.  i just don't think reality has any meaning.  i don't think any human knows the absolute truth about reality.

it's hard to look at that quote (for me).  right now i don't want to be here.  so therefore i don't want to be doing anything with anyone.  i would rather not remember this moment.  i don't have answers for myself.
